algorithm_verdict_basis.conflicting_criteria_detail: On the M2 paired common sample the primary metric PR-AUC excludes zero for no family, while Brier excludes zero for all three but in conflicting directions (random_forest worse, logistic and xgboost better). A criterion that disagrees with the primary metric cannot break a tie no frozen rule authorizes breaking.

explicit_prohibition_citations.binding_phrase: This evidence does NOT justify changing the primary result, selecting a winning model family, retuning any configuration, opening the final test, or automatically freezing a retained design.
paper_winner_selection and final_model_selection are listed among authorization_scope.not_authorized

algorithm_verdict_basis.frozen_rule_absent_detail: No committed frozen artifact contains a rule that maps development results to a single final algorithm. The metrics/uncertainty contract fixes primary_metric = PR-AUC for REPORTING and fixes a tie_break only for the thresholded secondary threshold choice (thresholded_secondary.tie_break = higher_threshold), not for model choice. Its only winner-related clause is a prohibition (do_not_select_winner_on_calibrated_final_test = true). No model-level tie-breaker exists anywhere.
algorithm_verdict_basis.retained_families_detail: The retained design freeze retains ALL THREE model families with their frozen configurations and sets final_model_selected = false. A selected configuration per algorithm is not a selected final algorithm.
algorithm_verdict_basis.confirmatory_family_1_detail: The frozen contract defines confirmatory_family_1 = [Logistic_vs_RF, Logistic_vs_XGBoost, RF_vs_XGBoost] under Holm at alpha 0.05. That family was never executed, so no adjusted inferential ranking of the three algorithms exists.

block_verdict_basis.frozen_rule_absent_detail: No committed frozen artifact contains a rule that selects a final predictor block. The nested confirmatory chain [M1, M2, M3, M4] defines an ARCHITECTURE and a comparison order; it does not designate a final block. Nothing states that the absence of M2 superiority forces M1, and nothing states that M2 retention forces M2. Choosing either would be inference, not rule-following.
block_verdict_basis.unresolved_interpretation: The frozen contracts are silent on final-block selection. This is an ABSENCE of a rule, not a conflict between rules, so the verdict is a human decision rather than a contract conflict.

M2_minus_M1.p_value_note: No Holm-adjusted or raw p-value is committed for this comparison. The committed evidence is paired cluster-bootstrap percentile-95 confidence intervals, quoted verbatim in the reconciliation artifact. This audit computes none.

holm_reporting_verdict_basis.detail: The frozen multiplicity contract fixes the family membership, the correction (Holm) and alpha (0.05), and forbids additional post hoc families. It is silent on how to close or report a family two of whose three prespecified members were never executed. The Stage129 M4 reporting decision settled how the M4 comparison is PRESENTED, not how the family is CLOSED.

questions_answered.q1_eligible_blocks_after_m3_m4_decisions: M1 and M2 only. M3-CBI and M4 were both discontinued before admission and before any modeling.
questions_answered.q2_does_m2_retained_mean_m2_selected: No. The merged retention decision states explicitly that retention does not imply final_model_selection or paper_winner_selection, and that its basis is architecture preservation, not observed predictive superiority.
questions_answered.q3_does_absent_m2_superiority_force_m1: No frozen rule says so. The contracts are silent on what block is selected when superiority is absent, so this cannot be resolved by rule-following.
questions_answered.q4_do_frozen_rules_determine_a_unique_al: No. There is no model-selection rule and no model-level tie-breaker; the retained design freeze retains all three families; and confirmatory_family_1, the only prespecified inferential ranking mechanism, was never executed.
questions_answered.q5_effect_of_robustness_and_ordering_ins: Part 1 fully reverses the primary ordering and Part 5 inverts the top two families within fold 1, so the ordering is not stable enough for a rule that does not exist to be applied deterministically even if one did.
questions_answered.q6_can_selection_proceed_without_new_hum: No. Both the block and the algorithm require a separate human decision.
